title: €1.9 Billion Vanished. It Never Existed. #shorts
description:
In 2020, Wirecard, a German payments giant in the DAX, admitted that 1.9 billion euros in cash probably never existed. Fake bank documents, a regulator that went after reporters, and a fugitive executive.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
first_comment: Who failed worse: the auditors who signed off for years, or the regulator who went after the reporters? 👇

lines.text: A German tech giant reported one point nine billion euros in cash. None of it existed.
The company was Wirecard, a payments star worth more than twenty billion euros.
In 2018, it even joined the DAX, Germany's top index.
But a reporter at the Financial Times kept digging.
He found its profits came from shadowy partners in Asia.
Instead of investigating Wirecard, Germany's regulator investigated the reporters.
Then, in June 2020, the auditors asked to see the cash.
It was supposedly held in two banks in the Philippines.
The banks said the documents were fake.
One week later, Wirecard went bankrupt. The first DAX company ever to do so.
The CEO was arrested. His number two vanished.
Jan Marsalek is still on the run, believed to be hiding in Russia.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
